description: 0/0 at a finite point using a Pythagorean/trig identity (e.g. sin^2x-1, 1-cos^2x) to factor and cancel.

exercises.technique: 0/0 at x=pi/2. Use sin^2x-1=-cos^2x=-(1-sin x)(1+sin x), cancel the (1+sin x) factor with the denominator, leaving -(1-sin x); substitute sin(pi/2)=1.
0/0 at x=0. Write sin^2x=(1-cos x)(1+cos x) via the Pythagorean identity, so the expression becomes -(1)/(1+cos x); substitute cos 0=1.
0/0 at x=0. Replace 1-cos^2x with sin^2x (Pythagorean identity), cancel one factor of sin x, leaving -2x/sin x, then apply the standard sinc limit x/sin x → 1.

0/0 at x=-pi/2. Factor sin^4x-1=(sin^2x-1)(sin^2x+1)=-(1-sin x)(1+sin x)(sin^2x+1) via difference of squares plus the Pythagorean form. Cancel (1+sin x), leaving -1/[(1-sin x)(sin^2x+1)]; substitute sin(-pi/2)=-1.
0/0 at x=-pi/2. Factor numerator via Pythagorean identity: 1-sin^2x=(1-sin x)(1+sin x); factor 2 from denominator: 2(1+sin x). Cancel (1+sin x), leaving (1-sin x)/2; substitute sin(-pi/2)=-1.
